title: The Midnight Exchange
subtitle: Nothing disappears without a trace.
briefing: At 21:10, the lights went out at the Meridian Museum. Ninety seconds later, the Aster prototype was gone. Four people had access. Everyone has an alibi. Someone is lying. Follow the paper trail, question the suspects, and find out who made the exchange.

suspects.name: Mara Vale
suspects.quote: Some things belong in a museum. Others don't.
suspects.motive: Her exhibition was about to lose its funding.
suspects.alibi: Reports waiting in the main atrium.
suspects.statement: At 21:05 I was in the main atrium, waiting for the power to return. My badge is M-17 and my assigned locker is 04. The east gallery was closed for the evening. You can check the floor plan.

suspects.name: Elias Reed
suspects.motive: A private collector had offered to clear his debts.
suspects.alibi: Claims to have stayed in the east gallery.
suspects.statement: I was in the east gallery from 21:00 until the alarm. My badge, N-41, never left my pocket. Locker 12 stayed locked all night. If someone used either, it wasn't me.

suspects.name: June Park
suspects.quote: Look closely. The details always survive.
suspects.motive: She believed the prototype had been acquired illegally.
suspects.alibi: Reports waiting in the main atrium.
suspects.statement: At 21:05 I was in the main atrium, waiting for the power to return. My badge is C-26 and my assigned locker is 08. The east gallery was closed for the evening. You can check the floor plan.

suspects.name: Theo Cross
suspects.quote: I keep the lights on. That's the job.
suspects.motive: The museum had withheld three months of his pay.
suspects.alibi: Reports waiting in the main atrium.
suspects.statement: At 21:05 I was in the main atrium, waiting for the power to return. My badge is T-09 and my assigned locker is 21. The east gallery was closed for the evening. You can check the floor plan.

evidence.title: 90 seconds of darkness
evidence.label: EXHIBIT 01 · CCTV
evidence.body: The feed shows the east corridor before the blackout. The east gallery shutters are already down. The camera loses power at 21:10:00 and returns at 21:11:30. The archive door is open when the feed returns. No face is visible; this image alone identifies nobody.

evidence.title: The door remembers
evidence.label: EXHIBIT 02 · ACCESS LOG
evidence.summary: One badge. One very convenient visit.
evidence.body:
OFFLINE CONTROLLER EXPORT
21:07:51  MAIN ATRIUM   emergency lights ON
21:08:14  ARCHIVE A     badge N-41 — ACCESS GRANTED
21:10:00  CAMERA GRID   power lost
21:11:30  CAMERA GRID   power restored

The archive controller has a backup battery. Its records survived. A badge can be borrowed: corroborate this record with physical evidence.

evidence.title: A way out
evidence.label: EXHIBIT 03 · FLOOR PLAN
evidence.summary: The service corridor wasn't on the tour.
evidence.body: The archive connects to the cloakroom through a staff-only service corridor. The east gallery was shuttered at 20:45 and cannot be entered from that corridor. The main atrium remained open. A trip from archive to cloakroom takes approximately one minute.

evidence.title: A paper trail
evidence.label: EXHIBIT 04 · CLOAKROOM
evidence.summary: A transfer somebody hoped you'd miss.
evidence.body:
MERIDIAN CLOAKROOM — MANUAL TRANSFER
Item: ASTER / transport case 001
Destination: assigned locker 12
Received: 21:09
Seal: intact

The attendant saw the locker holder place the case inside, using their personal locker key. Locker assignments are listed in the suspect dossiers. The case was later recovered there, empty.

evidence.title: An unfinished message
evidence.label: EXHIBIT 05 · TRANSCRIPT
evidence.summary: “We only need a minute and a half.”
evidence.body:
Recovered voicemail transcript, 20:38:
"The cameras don't have backup power. We only need a minute and a half. The service corridor gets us to the lockers. Don't call me again."

The recording is distorted. The caller cannot be identified by voice. It establishes preparation and the intended route, not the caller's identity.

evidence.title: More than a prototype
evidence.label: EXHIBIT 06 · CURATOR'S NOTE
evidence.summary: An object with a complicated past.
evidence.body: The Aster prototype was due to be unveiled tomorrow. Its ownership is disputed; its insurance valuation is substantial. An unsigned note reads: "Before you ask who wanted it, ask who could actually move it." Several suspects had motives. Motive alone is not proof.

solution.explanation: Elias Reed's badge (N-41) opened the archive at 21:08. Independently, the cloakroom attendant recorded the Aster case entering his assigned locker (12) at 21:09, in his presence. Together these contradict his claim of remaining in the shuttered east gallery. Neither motive nor the anonymous voicemail identifies the culprit by itself.
